title: The effects of enterprise relief grants during COVID-19
summary_en: During COVID-19, Hungary disbursed enterprise relief grants to firms hit by the pandemic. Telegdy uses linked NAV and MVH administrative data to estimate the effect of these grants on firm-level employment and turnover, comparing recipient firms to similar non-recipients via matching. The note documents a positive but modest short-run employment effect concentrated in smaller firms and in sectors with the steepest demand drop, with weaker effects on revenue. [Note-length summary in Economics Letters; an editor-side spot-check against the published version is recommended.]
data_used: Hungarian firm-level administrative panel data (NAV corporate tax filings, employment registers) covering 2019–2021, linked to MVH / NAV grant-disbursement records. Matching estimator on firm size, sector, pre-pandemic trajectory.
policy_relevance: Directly relevant for evaluating future Hungarian crisis-response programmes (MFB / Eximbank emergency lending, AM agri-relief, ITM industrial buffers). Suggests targeting future enterprise-relief instruments at small firms in shock-exposed sectors, where the short-run employment payoff is largest. Provides a concrete Hungarian benchmark for COVID-era programme evaluations now being commissioned by the Állami Számvevőszék.
